small_guidance:
- Try larger BLOCK_OC (64) with TILE_PH=2, TILE_PW=8 (CONV tile 8x32) and num_warps=4 to reduce register pressure while keeping good GEMM-K reuse; also sweep BLOCK_OC=64/TILE=(4,8) and BLOCK_OC=32/TILE=(8,8).
- Wrap launch in `triton.autotune` over `{BLOCK_OC, TILE_PH, TILE_PW} x {num_warps in [4,8]} x {num_stages in [2,3,4]}` keyed on (N, OC, OH, OW) so the best tile is picked automatically.
- The inner `(BLOCK_OC, SPAT)` outer-product is essentially a GEMM; consider laying out the loops so the IC*KH*KW axis is the K-reduction explicitly and use `tl.dot` with a (BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_K) x (BLOCK_K, SPAT) tile to leverage tensor cores (cast accumulator-input to fp16/bf16 if accuracy holds, or use tf32).
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as an im2col-style GEMM using `tl.dot`: pack weights as (OC, IC*KH*KW) and gather an (IC*KH*KW, SPAT) input tile per program; one program per (N, OC_tile, output-spatial tile), with the pool reduction fused at the epilogue. Tensor-core dot will be substantially faster than the current scalar FMA outer-product loop.
- Switch input/weight to channels-last (NHWC) so the GEMM-K (IC) dimension is contiguous; this makes the im2col gather coalesce and removes the strided IC*IH*IW jumps in the current kernel.
- Increase the spatial tile so that one program does a meaningful chunk of output (e.g. CONV_TH=8, CONV_TW=32 → 8x32=256 conv outputs producing 2x8 pooled outputs) and use persistent-grid / split-K only if K (IC*KH*KW=72) becomes a bottleneck — here K is small so a single-pass dot is ideal.
